Edit this photograph, picture 1. Change only the birds roped on the back and the one at the chest, which become carved wooden decoys. Everything else stays exactly as it is, in the same place and at the same size: Lunari Hollowreach, the face, the hands, the clothes, the place and every light that falls on them.

THE DECOYS. Every bird Lunari Hollowreach carries is a carved wooden decoy, plainly made by hand, and none is a real bird. Each is one solid piece of carved wood: a smooth simplified body with no separate feathers, the head and the long neck carved in one piece with it, the feather pattern only painted on in a few flat strokes of dull brown, grey and cream, worn away to bare pale wood at the bill, the crown of the head and every edge, with the grain of the wood showing through and fine cracks along it. The eyes are small painted dots. The heads are all held at the same stiff upright angle, the bills shut, because they are carved. A brass screw-eye is set in the breast of each, and the rope runs through the screw-eyes from one decoy to the next. They are roped in the same places as the birds now, as many and the same size, riding high on the back and shoulders behind the ears.

The one at the chest hangs upside down on its rope, so its underside faces the camera: a flat wooden base with a dark lead keel weight screwed along it. Rain beads on the painted wood and runs off it, and the lightning glints on the wet paint as it does now.

It stays one photograph taken with a real camera: the new parts have the grain, the focus and the exposure of the rest and meet it without a seam. Nothing in the picture carries writing, numbers or a symbol.
